items.caseName: Sucheta Dalal v. Union of India
items.coram: Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R. Mahadevan
items.headline: Sucheta Dalal's PIL on unclaimed financial assets closed; concerns 'substantially addressed'
items.text: The Court disposed of the 2022 PIL seeking a single searchable system to help legal heirs trace unclaimed deposits, shares and other assets of deceased persons. It found that steps taken by the Centre, RBI and SEBI, including the UDGAM and MITRA portals, had substantially met the petition's concerns, so judicial directions were not needed. Specific grievances can go to the competent authority, and the petitioner may take her Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund grievance to the Social Justice Ministry.
items.why: Leaves the tracing of over ₹1 lakh crore in unclaimed assets to the regulators' portals rather than court monitoring.

items.caseName: Hindu Dharma Parishad v. Union of India
items.coram: Justice Aravind Kumar, Justice Vipul Pancholi
items.headline: Thiruparankundram: lamp to be lit at Deepathoon on 28 Nov; temple trustees suspended, contempt notices to TN officials
items.text: Finding a prima facie wilful breach of its 20 November order, the Court directed that the lamp be lit at the Deepathoon on 28 November, opened lighting to all devotees at least 50 metres from the Dargah, and placed the temple and Dargah under CRPF security. It suspended the temple's Board of Trustees, appointed two former Madras High Court judges as receivers and vacated its stay on the High Court's Deepathoon findings. Thirteen officials and trustees, including the Chief Secretary and DGP, must show cause against contempt and appear in person on 15 December.
items.why: A strong assertion that all authorities must act in aid of the Supreme Court under Article 144.

items.caseName: Naresh Balyan v. NCT of Delhi
items.coram: Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh
items.headline: Former AAP MLA Naresh Balyan granted bail in MCOCA case
items.text: The Court granted bail to Naresh Balyan, accused of facilitating gangster Kapil Sangwan's extortion syndicate, setting aside the Delhi High Court's 3 August refusal. He has been in custody since December 2024 and must cooperate fully with the trial, failing which bail may be withdrawn.

items.caseName: Deepak Singla v. Directorate of Enforcement
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: AAP leader Deepak Singla gets interim bail in ₹155-crore bank fraud PMLA case
items.text: Noting over six months in custody and bail to a co-accused, the Court granted Singla interim bail and declined the ED's request for a deposit as a condition. The Punjab and Haryana High Court was asked to decide his regular bail plea within a fixed time, without being influenced by this order. Reports differ on whether the period is three or four weeks.

items.caseName: Himanshu Shekhar @ Mohit v. Directorate of Enforcement
items.coram: Justice M.M. Sundresh, Justice P.B. Varale
items.headline: Mahadev app case: notice on Delhi lawyer's plea against re-arrest, no interim protection
items.text: The Court issued notice to the ED on a lawyer's challenge to the Bombay High Court order of 23 November that allowed his fresh arrest in the Mahadev betting app money-laundering case. It refused interim protection. The ED alleges he took over ₹15 crore to influence judges and officials, which he denies.

items.caseName: Khalid Jahangir Qazi v. Union of India
items.coram: Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Union asked to consider restricted entry for blacklisted US-based OCI cardholder
items.text: The Court asked the Union to consider letting an elderly US-based professor, whose OCI card was cancelled and who was blacklisted over alleged anti-India activities, enter India with restrictions, perhaps confined to the town where his sisters live. It noted that a Delhi High Court single-judge ruling quashing the blacklisting remains unstayed, and adjourned the matter by a week for the Union's instructions.

items.caseName: Zahid Ali v. Union of India
items.coram: Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh
items.headline: Plea to remove videos of Italian politician's 'Vote Chor' slogan at Bharat Summit dismissed
items.text: The Court dismissed a plea seeking takedown of videos of European socialist leader Giacomo Filibeck raising the 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' slogan at the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, and curbs on speeches at events with foreign guests. The Bench said the petitioner was free to make a representation to the authorities.

items.caseName: Durvesh Kumar v. State of UP
items.coram: Justice Salil Kumar Rai and Justice Padam Narain Mishra
items.headline: Man on death row for killing his parents acquitted over contradictory eyewitness accounts
items.text: The Bench set aside the conviction and death sentence imposed in January 2024 for the 2020 shooting of the appellant's parents in Bareilly. It found the two eyewitnesses contradicted each other on the time and sequence of the attack and on when their statements were recorded, and held that the recovery of a pistol and clothing could not cure these gaps. The death reference was rejected.
items.why: A reminder that a death sentence cannot rest on eyewitness testimony riddled with material inconsistencies.

items.caseName: Hausila Prasad Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Revenue Lko and 8 Others
items.coram: Justice Jaspreet Singh
items.headline: Revenue officials faulted for aiding encroachers on public land; Sultanpur Collector to probe forged entries
items.text: Hearing a PIL on encroachment of public utility land in Sajampur village, Sultanpur, the Court said officials claiming 'zero tolerance' were in fact aiding encroachers. It directed the Collector to investigate suspected tampering of revenue records and to file a personal affidavit on the extent of such land and pending eviction orders. The petitioner was fined Rs 10,000 for hiding his own encroachment, and the case is listed on 11 December.

items.caseName: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Krishnapriya S. Pappu & Others
items.coram: Justice B. Krishna Mohan and Justice Alapati Giridhar
items.headline: Income tax and professional tax must be deducted from a deceased's salary when computing accident compensation
items.text: The Bench held that tax deductions must come off the deceased's salary before loss of dependency is worked out. Recomputing with a multiplier of 14 and 25% future prospects, it cut the award from about Rs 2.32 crore to Rs 1.91 crore. The insurer's appeal was partly allowed, with interest at 7.5% a year.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Abhay Ahuja
items.headline: No interim relief to Tata Trusts; Tata Sons' 30 November board meeting may go ahead
items.text: The Tata Trusts are challenging Tata Sons' 17 September board resolution reappointing N. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman. The Court refused to stay the 30 November board meeting but made it subject to the outcome of the petitions, and gave the respondents time to reply. The matter is next listed on 21 January 2027.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Krishna Rao
items.headline: Ritabrata Banerjee's appointment as West Bengal Leader of Opposition set aside
items.text: On a petition by TMC leader Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, the Court quashed the Speaker's decision to recognise Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of Opposition, and Akhruzzaman's appointment as the TMC's Chief Whip. It found the Speaker had not acted impartially, and directed him to decide afresh within ten days.
items.why: Courts can review a Speaker's recognition of the Leader of Opposition where the process is shown to be partisan.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Sachin Datta
items.headline: Notice to Satyendar Jain on ACB's plea to cancel his bail in Jal Board corruption case
items.text: The Anti-Corruption Branch challenges the trial court's grant of bail to the AAP leader in the alleged Delhi Jal Board sewage treatment plant scam. It argues the trial court gave too much weight to the absence of a direct money trail and ignored the risk of witnesses being influenced. The matter is listed on 22 December.

items.caseName: Shashank Deo Sudhi v. Delhi High Court Bar Association & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Amit Mahajan
items.headline: Delhi High Court Bar Association is not a 'public authority' under the RTI Act
items.text: The Court refused to declare the Bar Association a public authority or to direct it to appoint a CPIO. Following a Division Bench ruling that bar associations are private bodies outside writ jurisdiction, it disposed of the advocate's petition.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.coram: Justice Jasmeet Singh
items.headline: Notice on law student's challenge to BCI circular restricting internships to vacations
items.text: A fourth-year law student challenges the Bar Council of India's 2014 circular allowing internships only during vacations, saying it goes beyond the 2008 Rules of Legal Education. He also contests his institute's refusal of a no-objection certificate for a February 2027 internship. Responses were sought from the BCI, GGSIP University and Maharaja Surajmal Institute, and the case is listed on 27 January 2027.

items.caseName: Joyce Oyella v. Customs
items.coram: Justice Girish Kathpalia
items.headline: Customs pulled up for 'lackadaisical approach' in opposing heroin smuggling accused's bail
items.text: Customs had not placed its status report on record over several hearings, and the investigating officer stayed away despite an earlier order. The Court gave a final opportunity, sought a report from the Registrar General on the filing lapse, and sent its order to the Commissioner of Customs. The bail plea is listed on 14 December.

items.caseName: Neera Suri v. Jagjit Singh Sawhney (Since Deceased) Thr LRs & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar
items.headline: MCD receipts, municipal letters and electricity bills don't prove ownership of property
items.text: The appellant claimed a second-floor property through her late mother and relinquishment deeds from her sisters. The Court dismissed her appeal under Order XXI Rule 58 CPC, holding that municipal and utility documents do not establish title and that she had not shown the source of the rights she claimed.

items.caseName: Prince Chacko v. State of Kerala and Ors.
items.coram: Dr. Justice A.K. Jayasankaran Nambiar and Justice Syam Kumar V.M.
items.headline: PIL against tranquilising wild elephant 'Chakkakomban' dismissed; petitioner's bona fides doubted
items.text: The Bench found the PIL frivolous, with no wider public interest or urgency, and noted the petitioner filed in a personal capacity from Kottayam. Relying on the Chief Wildlife Warden's statement that the operation was for radio-collaring and that corridor concerns were being addressed, it treated the issues as no longer live. Bona fide petitioners may still raise the cause.

items.caseName: P.M. Rajan v. State of Kerala
items.coram: Justice A. Badharudeen
items.headline: Strong suspicion of conspiracy enough to refuse discharge, even without direct evidence
items.text: The second accused in a vigilance case over land bought under a tribal welfare scheme sought discharge. Rs 77 lakh was allegedly paid for 200 cents when only 183.5 cents were held, causing an excess payment of about Rs 11.49 lakh. Upholding the Special Judge's refusal of discharge, the Court held that strong suspicion is sufficient to send the case to trial.

items.caseName: Abibash P.S. v. Principal District Judge, Palakkad and Others
items.coram: Justice Gopinath P.
items.headline: Sanctioning posts for new NDPS courts doesn't create vacancies before the courts start functioning
items.text: Ranked-list candidates for Confidential Assistant Grade-II sought reporting of vacancies in new NDPS Special Courts before their lists lapsed on 30 November. The Court held that a Government Order sanctioning posts does not by itself create reportable vacancies until a commencement notification is issued. Their three writ petitions were dismissed, as ranked candidates have no indefeasible right to appointment.

items.caseName: M.S. Anil v. State of Kerala and Ors.
items.coram: Justice A. Badharudeen
items.headline: SNDP microfinance fraud: State assures an uninfluenced probe; all final reports in three weeks
items.text: After the Court questioned investigating officer S. Sasidharan IPS in person and voiced concern about possible pressure on him, the State assured it that the Rs 15.85 crore probe would not be interfered with. The State said all remaining final reports would be filed within three weeks. The Court granted the time and posted the case to 7 December.

items.caseName: Ramjeet v. State of MP
items.coram: Justice G.S. Ahluwalia and Justice Anuradha Shukla
items.headline: Gwalior SSP slammed over denial of police escorts for a cancer-stricken prisoner; AAG office warned
items.text: The central jail sent 34 requisitions for escorts to take a cancer-stricken prisoner to AIIMS, and most went unanswered. The Bench found the Reserve Inspector had denied receiving them and filed a misleading reply, and it criticised the SSP for shielding officials. The Inspector and a constable were suspended pending inquiry, and the order was sent to the Chief Minister and Chief Secretary. The Court also warned the AAG's office to file documents shown to the court the same day or explain why not.

items.caseName: Child In Conflict With Law v. State of MP
items.coram: Justice Alok Awasthi
items.headline: NDPS bail curbs can't displace the special bail test for juveniles under the JJ Act
items.text: A child aged about 17 years and 5 months was caught with an adult co-accused carrying 20.6 kg of poppy straw, and was refused bail by the Board and the appellate court. The Court held that Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice Act governs a child's bail, not the stricter NDPS conditions. Noting the child was not a habitual offender and the quantity was below commercial level, it allowed the revision.

items.caseName: C. Joseph Vijay v. S. Dinesh
items.coram: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan
items.headline: CM Vijay's plea to reject election petition against his Perambur win dismissed
items.text: The Court held that the voter's election petition discloses a cause of action and is maintainable. It found the alleged discrepancies in Vijay's nomination affidavit were specifically pleaded and must be tested at trial. The petition alleges undue influence under Section 123(2) of the Representation of the People Act, which the Chief Minister denies.

items.caseName: Venkatachalapathy v. ECI
items.coram: Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan
items.headline: Bypolls allowed in Ambasamudram and Perundurai; Tiruchi East, Viralimalai and Karur deferred
items.text: On a PIL, the Division Bench allowed by-elections in two seats vacated by AIADMK MLAs who joined TVK. Bypolls in Tiruchi East (vacated by CM Vijay), Viralimalai and Karur must wait until election courts decide the pending petitions challenging the earlier results, including prayers under Section 84 of the Representation of the People Act.

items.caseName: Vinod Dhattewal and Others v. Union of India and Others
items.coram: Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Sanjiv Berry
items.headline: High Court tells Centre it cannot recommend new judges for want of courtrooms
items.text: Hearing a PIL by a court employee, the Court noted that it has 85 sanctioned judges but only 69 courtrooms, which is stalling recommendations for appointment. It asked the Additional Solicitor General to press the Union Home Secretary for urgent action. It held that the High Court, not the government, decides what infrastructure it needs.
items.why: Infrastructure shortfalls are now directly holding up judicial appointments at one of India's busiest High Courts.
